messages:
sam: Quick RFC follow-up. We saw a revoke -> immediate cross-shard re-admit pattern causing eviction storms. Need a lightweight handoff so a revoke is respected cluster-wide.
anya: Is the issue that revokes write to KV but other schedulers read lazily? :confused:
sam: Yep. By the time another shard grants a lease, revoke hasn't propagated and client bounces around schedulers.
kai: Proposal: short-lived tombstone in KV + local LRU cache + optional fanout ping. Admission flow: local token fast-path, consult cache, if miss async KV read and put client into probation path while we fetch.
anya: That avoids blocking happy path. Metrics we should capture: tombstone read QPS, cache hit ratio, new-lease-after-revoke rate, probation admissions.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: revocation-cache + probation fallback to 20% nodes at 01:30 UTC for 90m.
sam: Also need appeal/rollback flow for false positives. Ops manual retract + automated appeals put tenant in probation instead of immediate full restore.
kai: Implementation note: tombstone key `revoke:{tenant}:{seq}`; cache stores highest seq seen. Keep TTL short (15-60s). I'll prototype cache + async fetch.
anya: Action items: kai -> prototype + perf test; sam -> micro-RFC with TTL and probation rates; ops -> draft retract playbook. We'll reconvene after canary.
